scope: Corollary 1.3 (Satisfiable Not-Two and three-query PCPs) of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let NTW(a, b, c) be the Boolean predicate accepting exactly zero, one, or three true inputs. For every fixed 0 < ε < 3/8, it is NP-hard to distinguish a satisfiable instance with constraints NTW(ℓ1, ℓ2, ℓ3) from one in which every assignment satisfies at most a 5/8 + ε fraction of the constraints; each literal ℓi may be a variable or its negation. Consequently, every language in NP has a polynomial-time verifier using O(log n) random bits and three nonadaptive proof-bit queries, with perfect completeness and soundness at most 5/8 + ε, where n is the input length.
